allow_large: The owner picked this fix on 2026-09-29 (Forge's repo runs current code); its only home is the command entry in src/forge/cli.py, which the hook treats as an interface file
done_when: In Forge's own repo, a forge command whose installed code differs from the checkout's src/forge runs the checkout's own code instead, and says so once; a test runs forge from an older install inside a newer checkout and sees the checkout's version answer

findings.body: The redirect trusts a repository's own `forge.toml` value `repo = "forge-source"` and the presence of `src/forge`. An unrelated Git repository can supply both, causing even `forge --version` to launch Python with that repository's `src` on `PYTHONPATH` and import its code. The guard needs a way to identify Forge's own checkout before executing checkout code.
findings.title: Unrelated repositories can make forge execute their Python code

findings.body: An installation made before this fix has the old `cli.py`, whose `_run` goes straight to argument parsing; it never executes this new redirect. Invoking that installed command inside a newer checkout therefore still runs the installed code and gives its installed version. This fails the requested older-install behavior, even though the branch's test passes.
findings.title: Not done: An older installed Forge must run the checkout's code and announce it

findings.body: `_forge_code(install, "1.0.0")` copies this branch's current `src/forge` into the simulated install and changes only its version string. Both copies therefore contain the new redirect. The test does not run code from an older installation and cannot catch the failure of a pre-fix installed command to switch to the checkout.
findings.title: Not done: Test with an actual older Forge installation

findings.body: The close run reports `test_5_forge_stays_small` failing: `src/forge` has 8,005 lines against the 8,000-line ceiling in `pyproject.toml`. The alias removal did not bring the branch below the ceiling. This added entry-point code leaves the repository's required test suite failing.
findings.title: The added code breaks Forge's 8,000-line test

why: In Forge's own repo a forge installed earlier from the checkout keeps running old code after changes merge, so it can write reviews in an old format that CI rejects
